National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
1251 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonably hot with highs in the 90s and heat index values
  100-107F each day.
  
- An isolated late day shower can't be ruled out along the
  seabreeze later today and Wednesday, but most locations will 
  remain dry.
  
- Slightly better rain chances expected Thursday into early next
  week for southern parts of the region as some deeper moisture
  flows back inland. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1251 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

No significant changes were made to the ongoing forecast. With 
the exception of an isolated seabreeze/baybreeze shower or 
thunderstorm, subsidence and modest moisture levels should keep 
rain chances fairly low for the vast majority of the region. As
the days progress Thursday into early next week, we should see
heights fall just a touch across our coastal areas as the western
ridge repositions just a bit further north. This, along with a
developing fetch of SE llvl winds and higher PW's should allow for
some better rain chances (mainly just scattered diurnally driven 
coverage) for our southern 2-3 tiers of counties. High temperatures
should trend down a few degrees as well with the SE flow and more
cloud cover. 47

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 1251 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

Mainly clear skies prevail keeping conditions VFR for the afternoon 
and evening hours. A PROB30 for SH remains over IAH, HOU, and SGR
between 21z today and 01z tomorrow, there is still a less than 
10% chance of TS. Winds will begin to relax to LGT and VRB around 
5-7z across the terminals. This signals for the potential of 
another round of patchy mist/fog west of I-45 bringing MVFR 
VIS/CIG. CIG/VIS return to VFR after 1500z aided by the increasing
SSE winds. Wednesday afternoon conditions remain similar to today
bringing the possible for afternoon SH/TS. CW

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1251 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

Typical summertime pattern will prevail with onshore winds peaking
in the 10-15kt range and seas generally 2-4ft. Rain chances will
slightly increase Thursday into early next week...mainly isolated
to scattered activity in the late night through early afternoon 
hours for the coastal waters. 47

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
634 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A typical summer weather pattern will prevail through this week 
with a few afternoon thunderstorms each day. 

- Afternoon highs will climb into the low to mid 90s each day 
  with maximum heat indices ranging from 101 to 109.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Monday)
Issued at 1213 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

The dog days of summer are upon us and the weather 
pattern seems to have gotten the message as a persistent and 
somewhat stagnant weather pattern is expected to continue through 
the week. The area will remain sandwiched between a sprawling upper 
level ridge that continues to bake the southwestern U.S. and an 
upper level low centered over the southeastern U.S. The resulting 
weak gradient aloft will allow for daily, diurnally driven afternoon 
thunderstorms (20-40% chance). Any storms that develop will likely 
have little forward motion and will, instead, be propagated by 
outflow boundaries and the daily sea breeze. At the surface, weak 
high pressure over the central and eastern gulf will maintain light 
southerly winds through the weekend. Temperatures will remain near 
seasonal normals with afternoon highs climbing into the low to mid 
90s each day with maximum heat indices ranging from 101-109. 

Jones

&&

been fading over the past hour. Once the sunsets convection will
quickly dissipate. Near sunrise patchy fog will be a concern
otherwise VFR conditions will persist through the TAF period. 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1213 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

Light south to southwest flow will prevail through the 
weekend along with seas of 1-3 feet. Precipitation chances will 
range from 10-20% each afternoon.

&&

Issued at 1213 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

KBDI values continue to climb, sitting between 500 to 600. The 
somewhat lower dewpoints and humidity have departed with minimum

the rest of the week. Scattered daily afternoon thunderstorms 
(20-40%) are expected each day through the weekend.
